newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: GOVERNMENT CALLS INQUIRY INTO TOWERS REPORT
The Federal Government says it takes very seriously a report which shows possible links between childhood leukaemia and telecommunications towers.
Research published in the Medical Journal of Australia suggests children living near the towers may suffer two and a half times the normal rate of leukaemia.
Science and Technology Minister Peter McGauran has called an immediate inquiry and a review of scientific research already conducted.
Mr McGauran says while the Government doesn't want to create undue panic, people have aright to know if the towers are safe.
The Government says Australia will use World Health Organisation regulations, to determine safe levels of radiation emissions.
CLOSURE OF SAWMILLS IN NSW
The forestry industry says today's closure of three sawmills and a manufacturing company in New South Wales must not be the start of a trend.

Robert Bain, of the National Association of Forest Industries, says mills at Tenterfield, Glenn Innes and Mount George are being forced to close because of State Government policies, with the flow-on closure of a board plant at Wingham.
Dr Bain says his association had been working with the Federal and State Governments on the regional forest agreement process which was to scientifically assess the industry.
EVANS RESIGNED TO LOSING TELSTRA VOTE
Shadow Treasurer, Gareth Evans, says holds no hope of the two independent Senators changing their minds when the Senate takes the final vote on the part-sale of Telstra.
The vote is due later today or tomorrow.
The two independents have indicated they will vote with the Government to approve the part-sale.
Mr Evans says he holds little hope that either Tasmanian independent Brian Harradine or former long-serving Labor Senator, now independent, Mal Colston, will reverse their positions.
NT GOVT TO FOCUS ON ANDREWS BILL IN SENATE
Northern Territory Chief Minister Shane Stone says he's hopeful the Andrews bill will be strongly contested when it comes before the Senate in the new year.
Federal MPs are this afternoon expected to vote on the Andrews bill which aims to overturn the Territory's voluntary euthanasia law.
Mr Stone says the passage of the bill through the House of Representatives is all but assured.
He says the Territory Government will continue to make representations to the Senate and to the special senate committee that will travel to the Territory to examine the issue.
PEOPLE MAY HAVE TO PAY FOR BEACHES, CLAIMS STONE
Northern Territory Chief Minister Shane Stone says he believes people may have to pay for access to picnic spots and beaches in Darwin if the Native Title Claim over the city is successful.
A claim by the Larrakia people over parks, beaches, reserves and undeveloped crown land was officially lodged with the Native Title Tribunal last week.
Mr Stone says his concerns are based on the fact non-aboriginal residents pay an annual fee of 50-dollars per family, to use beaches on Aboriginal land in Nhulunbuy, on the Territory's eastern coast.
UNION DEFENDS STRIKE ACTION
Tens of thousands of university students across the country are facing missing out on enrolling for courses and scholarships next year.
Academics at eight universities in New South Wales, Queensland, Victoria and South Australia are refusing to mark exams and assignments or release the results.
They're pushing for wage rises of up to 20-percent.
At Sydney University, the industrial action has already resulted in the cancellation of the Dentistry Graduating Ceremony.
But Chris Holly from the National Tertiary Education Union has defended the action.
COLLINGWOOD TO INVESTIGATE FRACAS
The Collingwood Football Club today will begin an investigation into allegations that three players assaulted police over the weekend.
Aaron James, Jonathan Ross and Trent Hotton face charges after an alleged incident, around 12-30 on Sunday morning.
Police allege the footballers were wrestling on the footpath outside the Greater Union cinema in Russell Street when three police, including one female constable, intervened and were assaulted.
Collingwood President Kevin Rose says the incident will be thoroughly investigated.
